notes:
Lead work_id: lead-rfc5
mechanism_observation: request_bugfix PRE-STATE mis-stated BC_NAME_RE as consumed by validate(); it was dead code — The lead-rfc5 dispatch PRE-STATE asserted (empirically, citing ADR-018 D2 installed-package surface) that BC_NAME_RE at manifest.py:34 was 'consumed by validate() at manifest.py:170', so that 'bc-container manifest validate' rejected non-shopsystem names. Inspection of the installed bc_launcher.manifest.validate() body showed it never referenced BC_NAME_RE — the constant was a module-level dead constant only asserted against in tests/conftest.py (manifest-shape BDD that parses YAML directly, not via the controller). So validate() did NOT in fact reject non-shopsystem names before this change; the regex never gated the CLI path.\n\nWhy load-bearing: the request_bugfix sufficiency contract treats PRE-STATE as the empirical ground the ACCEPTANCE PIN tightens. Here the change was effectively additive-NEW behavior (wiring a name check into validate()) dressed as a tightening of existing behavior. The ACCEPTANCE PIN and revert-teeth still held — I wired the parameterized check INTO validate() so reverting to a hard 'shopsystem-' anchor turns the non-shopsystem scenario RED — but a future implementer who trusted the 'consumed by validate()' claim without verifying could have parameterized only the dead constant and shipped a no-op that still passed a naive 'shopsystem-* still validates' check. The general mechanism gap: PRE-STATE claims of 'constant X is consumed by function Y' should be verified against Y's body, not just the presence of constant X, before treating the surface as pinned-existing vs net-new.

publish-bc-base.yml fails at 'Set package visibility to public' (gh PATCH /user/packages/.../visibility -> 404) on every release v0.2.0-v0.2.5
description: CI DEFECT (recurring, all 6 releases red): publish-bc-base.yml build-and-push step SUCCEEDS (image is built + pushed to ghcr.io/dstengle/shopsystem-bc-base; v0.2.5 manifest returns HTTP 200, pullable with auth), but the job's overall conclusion is FAILURE because step 5 'Set package visibility to public' runs 'gh api --method PUT/PATCH /user/packages/container/shopsystem-bc-base/visibility -f visibility=public' and gets 'gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)'. Root cause: /user/packages/ is the wrong endpoint for this package's ownership, OR the GITHUB_TOKEN/actor lacks packages admin scope. Consequence for the fleet flip: the GHCR package may remain private, so 'docker pull ghcr.io/dstengle/shopsystem-bc-base:v0.2.5' requires registry auth rather than being anonymously pullable. FIX OPTIONS: (a) correct the endpoint to /orgs/{org}/packages/container/{pkg}/visibility or /user/... matching actual ownership; (b) grant the workflow a token with packages:write admin; (c) set the package public once manually in GHCR settings (visibility is sticky) and drop the step; (d) make the step non-fatal (|| true) if public-ness is handled out of band. Verified against run 27297009114 (v0.2.5) job 80632290637 step 5. Relates lead-if8q, lead-79kp.

mechanism_observation: Dispatch prose says '17 agent-vault scenarios' but scenarios[] payload carried 16 hashes — The lead-hxb8 request_bugfix description (and the prior lead-v4ih framing) repeatedly says '17 agent-vault scenarios'. The structured scenarios[] array actually dispatched on lead-v4ih carries exactly 16 hashes: 6952248a, f838de07, d6296d95, c4e88075, 3931e43e, 97734ca6, f23dfbe8, 6cb07698, 3b2a81c1, f73afae0, 64aaff80, 2a4e9889, f1b70c2b, e4348b11, b8f2e121, ff1ee370.

Why load-bearing: work_done.scenario_hashes can only echo the hashes that were actually dispatched (16). If the lead reconciles against an expected count of 17, the attestation will look short by one even though every dispatched scenario was implemented and is green. This is a prose-vs-payload count mismatch in the dispatch mechanism, not a missing scenario. Recommend the lead confirm whether a 17th scenario was intended (and dropped from the payload) or the prose count is simply off-by-one.

title: bd bootstrap derives new-issue prefix from db name not committed ids
description: lead-ezzr residual nit (NOT part of write-ready acceptance). The launcher provisions in-container beads via 'bd bootstrap' (controller.py ~line 850). bd bootstrap derives the new-issue prefix from the Dolt db name (e.g. 'scenarios') rather than from the committed issue ids (e.g. 'shopsystem-scenarios'). Minor consistency gap; bd remains fully functional (bd create / bd ready succeed, write-ready). Follow-up only. Surfaced during lead-ezzr request_bugfix.

title: Partial agent-vault triple + no explicit broker silently falls back to :14321 runtime HTTPS_PROXY instead of failing closed
description: Reviewer A3 finding on lead-3q12 (non-blocking, deferred by PO). _build_runtime_proxy_url (controller.py:261-307) derives the :14322 MITM proxy only when the FULL triple (AGENT_VAULT_ADDR/TOKEN/VAULT) is present and no explicit --agent-vault-broker is given. A PARTIAL triple (e.g. addr+token, vault missing) with no explicit broker returns None and falls back to bare broker_address (:14321 control API) at controller.py:640-645 — claude's brokered calls then fail at runtime (CONNECT 405) with NO launcher-side error. Matches pre-3q12 behavior (not a regression) and the HEALTHCHECK target, so left as-is for v0.2.6. Proposed tightening: launch should FAIL CLOSED naming the missing AGENT_VAULT_* key rather than ship a :14321 runtime proxy. PO (dave) to decide whether to pin. Relates lead-3q12, bclaunch-way.

title: Next bc-base release must include the bclaunch-wuo HEALTHCHECK (landed at 430579c, AFTER the v0.2.5 tag)
description: The real HEALTHCHECK (bclaunch-wuo, commit 430579c) was committed to origin/main AFTER the v0.2.5 tag was cut at 1b0ae92, so the published v0.2.5 bc-base image does NOT carry it (docker .State.Health stays 'none' on v0.2.5 containers). av1 item set 5-7 calls for image/runtime/health completeness in the RELEASED image. Cut a follow-up release (v0.2.6) from a HEAD that includes 430579c — bump pyproject + bc-base launcher pin to v0.2.6 — so the published image carries the HEALTHCHECK. Coordinate with bclaunch-lhh (visibility) so the rebuilt image is actually pullable. Relates av1, lead-if8q.
close_reason: Satisfied by v0.2.6: the bclaunch-wuo HEALTHCHECK (430579c) is folded into the v0.2.6 release (cut from a HEAD that includes it). bc-base pin + package version bumped to v0.2.6.

title: Tighten profile.d trust-var scenario: pin runtime env inheritance across tmux login-shell boundary, not static Dockerfile string
description: Review of agent-vault CA-env redesign (commits f1b85a8/df51d8d/25ac332) found that features/bc_base_agent_vault_entrypoint.feature scenarios (step defs conftest.py:4567-4626) only assert on static file content via read_text()+regex. The scenario 'the trust vars are durable for exec and login shells via /etc/profile.d' (feature line 41) asserts a profile.d script string exists in the Dockerfile but does NOT pin the actual runtime inheritance across the tmux login-shell boundary (controller.py:649-728 tmux new-session -> login bash -> sources /etc/profile.d/agent-vault-ca.sh -> send-keys 'agent-vault run -- claude'). Implementation is correct today, but a future controller.py change (e.g. tmux default-command 'bash --noprofile' or a non-login launch) would silently break TLS trust while leaving all 156 tests green. Add a Then step that exercises env inheritance through a login-shell sourcing of /etc/profile.d, OR pins that the controller tmux launch remains a login shell. Same tautological-pinning class as bclaunch-7ys.

title: Doc nit: clarify --agent-vault-broker (HTTPS_PROXY) vs env-file AGENT_VAULT_ADDR are separate channels, not an override
description: Reviewer of the critical-path work noted the help-text/commit wording 'explicit --agent-vault-broker wins over env-file AGENT_VAULT_ADDR' is imprecise. broker_address feeds HTTPS_PROXY (controller.py:442-446); env-file AGENT_VAULT_ADDR feeds the independent in-container agent-vault client var. Both independently controllable — code is correct; only the doc phrasing conflates them. Cosmetic.

value: This BC environment has NO GitHub push auth by default: no gh binary (yet 'gh auth git-credential' is the configured credential helper, so plain 'git push' fails), no GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN env var, no SSH key. To push you need an external credential — e.g. 'git -c credential.helper= push https://x-access-token:<PAT>@github.com/dstengle/shopsystem-bc-launcher.git HEAD:main'. The reviewer's pre-emit gate requires the work commit reachable on origin/main, so a missing push blocks sign-off until resolved.
